title: A check-in that waits on CI waits at most 55 minutes, read from one dated constant
why: A wake past the prompt cache lifetime pays to reload the whole context.
source: plan restart-plan (main), coordinator 11:46 CST Nov 12 for lane ruling-parts-cite-steps; R32 part 3 (owner pick c, Nov 11)
note: Rule git-ci-wait-checks-in ("each wider apart") becomes "each wider apart, never past 55 minutes". The cap is read from one constant that names its source and date (the prompt cache lifetime), so a change reaches every caller at once and the claim can be re-checked when it goes stale (owner: "we should keep some sort of tabs on how anthropic determiines warm cash so this doesn't go stale"). Ready, no lane. Lane ci-wait-cap-55 started 11:48 CST Nov 12 (coordinator): first checks the 55 against R3 (a total-time limit is read from green runs, never a stored number; step time-limits-end-hangs-only) and brings the coordinator any clash before building. Coordinator pick a 11:50 CST Nov 12: the 55 is a dated cache fact, not an R3 time limit, so the step builds as written. #2839 reopened after batch 104 merged (bcbeaa26a, 14:43 CST Nov 12); rebase on main and re-run lane-lint. Gap 00:39 CST Nov 14 (lane ci-wait-cap-55 via the coordinator, relayed): hooks/ci_wait_cap.json has no freshness check on its `read` date (R28 upkeep). The owner already asked for tabs on this fact ("keep some sort of tabs on how anthropic determiines warm cash so this doesn't go stale"), so triage reads it as part of this step's ask, not a new debt; the lane or the coordinator says if it is a follow-up step.
